## 1. AI Landing Page Builder or a Designed Landing Page? How to Choose for a Small Business Campaign
- Target keyword: AI landing page builder | Secondary: landing page vs website for small business, do I need a landing page
- Search intent: Commercial investigation
- Format: comparison / decision guide
- Angle: Form and survey tools now generate whole landing pages from a chat. Help an owner running one campaign (an ad, a seasonal offer, an event) decide when a generated page is enough, when it should live on their own site instead, and what a designer adds: message match with the ad, speed, tracking, and a page that keeps earning after the campaign ends.
- Why now: Typeform launched AI Landing Pages on 2026-10-06, generating publish-ready pages from a conversation with native forms and payments built in — https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/typeform-launches-ai-landing-pages-to-help-businesses-build-capture-and-convert-in-one-place-302899628.html
- Volume / KD: unverified
- Effort: Medium
- Outline starter:
  - H2: Landing page vs website: what each one is for
  - H2: What AI landing page builders can do now
  - H2: Where a generated page falls short (domain, tracking, speed, SEO)
  - H2: A quick decision rule: generated, on-site, or designed
  - H2: What to brief a designer if you hire one for a landing page

## 2. Do Your Brand Colors Pass WCAG Contrast? How to Keep Your Look and Fix the Failures
- Target keyword: website color contrast | Secondary: accessible brand colors, how to check color contrast on a website
- Search intent: Informational
- Format: how-to tutorial
- Angle: Contrast is the most common accessibility failure, and it usually comes from a brand palette, not careless pages. Show owners how to test their colors in a few minutes, why near-misses (just under 4.5:1) are fixed with a small shade change rather than a rebrand, and where a designer adjusts the system once so every page passes.
- Why now: An October 2026 axe-core test of 219 homepages found color contrast failing on 64.4% of them, with more than half of failing text measuring between 3.5:1 and 4.49:1 — https://bugviso.com/blog/website-accessibility-statistics-2026
- Volume / KD: unverified
- Effort: Low
- Outline starter:
  - H2: Why contrast is the most common accessibility failure
  - H2: The numbers that matter: 4.5:1, 3:1, and what they apply to
  - H2: How to test your brand colors in five minutes
  - H2: Fixing near-misses without a rebrand
  - H2: Buttons, links, and text on photos: the usual trouble spots

## 3. Contact Form Design for Small Business Websites: A 10-Point Checklist for More Inquiries
- Target keyword: contact form design best practices | Secondary: accessible contact form, how many fields should a contact form have
- Search intent: Informational
- Format: checklist
- Angle: The contact form is where most small business sites turn a visitor into a lead, and it's often the least designed part of the page. Give DIY owners a checklist (field count, labels, error messages, mobile tap targets, spam protection, confirmation step) and show what changes when a designer treats the form as part of the brand.
- Why now: WordPress 7.2 is now scheduled for 2026-12-08 with Beta 1 on 2026-10-20, and its roadmap adds styling of form elements in Global Styles, so DIY WordPress owners get new form design controls this cycle — https://make.wordpress.org/core/2026/10/06/wordpress-7-1-release-party-schedule-2/
- Volume / KD: unverified
- Effort: Low
- Outline starter:
  - H2: Why the contact form is your most important small design detail
  - H2: How many fields to ask for (and which to drop)
  - H2: Labels, errors, and focus states that work for everyone
  - H2: Mobile, spam protection, and the thank-you step
  - H2: What WordPress 7.2's form styling changes for DIY sites

## 4. Does Your Small Business Website Need an llms.txt File?
- Target keyword: llms.txt | Secondary: do I need llms.txt, llms.txt for small business website
- Search intent: Informational
- Format: FAQ explainer
- Angle: Website builders have started generating llms.txt files automatically, and owners are being told they need one. Explain in plain words what the file is, that it's a proposed convention rather than a standard, what Google has said about it, and why clear service pages and crawlable text matter more, so owners don't pay someone to "set up llms.txt" before the basics.
- Why now: A 2026-10-05 guide to Wix's GEO tools notes Wix now auto-generates llms.txt for upgraded sites, while Wix itself calls it "a proposed standard, not a formal one" — https://eseospace.com/blog/wix-ai-search-visibility/
- Volume / KD: unverified
- Effort: Low
- Outline starter:
  - H2: What an llms.txt file is (and isn't)
  - H2: Which builders create one for you
  - H2: What Google and AI assistants have said about it
  - H2: What actually helps AI tools describe your business
  - H2: Should you add, edit, or ignore it? A quick answer by site type

## 5. Learning SEO as a Beginner Web Designer: A 30-Day Plan Built on Google's Free Playlists
- Target keyword: SEO for web designers | Secondary: learn SEO for beginners, SEO basics for new web designers
- Search intent: Informational
- Format: learning roadmap / resource guide
- Angle: Aimed at the secondary audience of aspiring designers. Turn Google's two new curated playlists into a 30-day plan, pairing each week with one design decision it affects (headings, page structure, images, speed), so a new designer learns which SEO basics belong in the design and which belong to someone else.
- Why now: Google Search Central published two curated YouTube learning paths on 2026-10-06, one for Search fundamentals and one for Technical SEO — https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/10/seo-learning-paths
- Volume / KD: unverified
- Effort: Medium
- Outline starter:
  - H2: Why web designers need SEO basics before their first client
  - H2: Week 1: how Google finds and reads a page
  - H2: Week 2: structure, headings, and internal links in your layouts
  - H2: Week 3: images, speed, and mobile as design decisions
  - H2: Week 4: Search Console basics and what to hand off
  - H2: A pre-launch SEO checklist for your design projects
